headings: Bachelor of Science in Business Administration
The program is designed for USF undergraduate students who want legal fluency without a JD.
Learn the language that businesses speak — all over the world.
Create campaign strategies, media plans, performance analyses, and ads in every medium. Then go forth and persuade the world.
Explore Black American life through the study of history, literature, politics, theology, and arts. Examine inequality & join our pursuit of equity and justice.
Study the history and cultures of Africa and the African diaspora. This minor spans the humanities, social sciences, and African & African American literature.
Explore human behavior across cultures, in the context of humanity as a whole.
Architecture, community design, urban design, city planning, and landscape design — come study and practice design that makes a difference.
Blend history and theory with practical experience. Learn visual literacy, critical thinking, and research skills that enable you to thrive in the art world.
Connect with the beauty of the past. Study the art and architecture of cultures around the world and throughout time.
Explore Asian Pacific American art, health, communication & politics. Learn the APA legacy of struggle and APA contributions to American culture and democracy.
Understand Asia — study its histories, laws, economies, and governments, and also its philosophical, artistic, and intellectual foundations.

A minor in Biochemistry is an excellent program for students interested in healthcare and bioscience-related fields. This includes students preparing for medical school, pharmacy school, and graduate studies. These students often go on to pursue careers in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical sector.
Join a real-world research project led by a faculty member. Learn by doing. Get on the inside track for industry jobs or for medical and PhD programs.
Earn a BS in biology and a PSM degree in biotechnology in five years. Combine molecular biology with the business and soft skills you need to succeed.
Learn how business works. No matter what your career goals, knowing the foundations of business will give you an edge.
Learn advanced analytical tools to solve business problems.

Develop strong analytical foundations while advancing your capabilities in data management, coding, GenAI, and visualization. Ideal for students seeking leadership roles where strategic thinking meets technological execution.
Study Catholicism and explore its role in academics, the arts, and sciences, plus its relation to other religions. This minor complements any major.
Explore the chemical world in motion around us. Join real research projects led by faculty members.
Learn the physical, psychological, spiritual, social, and cultural aspects of human development during the first 18 years of life.
Learn to speak, read, and write Chinese, just minutes from the largest Chinatown outside of Asia. Prepare for a career in business, diplomacy, or hospitality.
Learn how we learned how to think. Use ancient languages, history, politics, philosophy, and literature to develop your own ideas about how the world works.
Our Clinical Nurse Leader (4+1) is a dual degree program that combines the BSN and the MSN into one program that saves you both time and tuition.
Major in communication studies then spend a final year getting your MA in professional communication with a health, strategic or technical communication concentration.
Discover how words, images, gestures, and symbols reflect and affect human behavior. Prepare to make a difference in a broad range of fields.
Computer Science/Computer Science, AI Concentration (4+1), BS/MS
Major in computer science as an undergraduate. Then spend a final year getting your MS in computer science with a concentration in AI.
Gain hands-on experience in small lecture-lab classes led by experts in the field. Benefit from learning in San Francisco — technology hub of the world.
Explore the cultural causes of crime and violence. Discover why get-tough programs fail and discuss what might work better.
Explore the social constructions of race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality, citizenship, and religion.
Come study dance, express your artistry, engage with the community, and take social action.
